title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This short page closes manuscript §3 (archive p.103 = MS p.51 bis), just before §4 'Sections d'extensions et anneaux de valuation généraux'.

On the previous page Grothendieck lists conditions a)-e) on a curve of type (g,ν) over a field with a valuation. a)⇒b)⇒c)⇒d) is evident. He expects d)⇒a) to be known or easy. These conditions imply e), but he does not see how e) implies good reduction. This is an Oda/Tamagawa-type criterion: good reduction read off from the Galois action on π1.

He then states a 'general principle'. Start from a curve of type (g,ν) over a field k of finite type over Q that 'reduces badly'. Pass to the degenerate (stable) fibre. Its profinite fundamental group is a 'π à lacets', a fundamental group carrying loops coming from the nodes, i.e. of a degenerate or graph-of-groups type. In this way one obtains fairly natural outer actions of Galois groups E_k = Gal(k̄/k) on such π à lacets, actions which are presumably not geometric.

This page continues: 'but I stop, not going down this road.' Two tasks are left open:
(i) make such actions effective (faithful);
(ii) an 'exercise': produce outer actions that are already geometric in some weaker sense (probably on the group level, or after restriction) but are not themselves geometric. 'Geometric' here means of one of the two types 1°, 2° described at the start of §3, which are not on this page.

In modern terms: produce non-geometric but 'nearly geometric' outer Galois representations on profinite surface groups, or on fundamental groups of stable curves, using degeneration. This bears on the problem of characterizing which outer Galois actions come from curves, a question at the heart of the anabelian programme.
errors: No mathematical claims are asserted, so there is nothing to check. Exact parsing of 'actions qui[?] effectives' and 'actions ext. déjà géométriques' is uncertain.

ideas.what: Use degeneration (bad reduction) of curves of type (g,ν) to obtain natural outer Galois actions on fundamental groups of degenerate curves ('π à lacets') that are not geometric
ideas.modern_name: outer Galois representations on fundamental groups of stable curves / semi-graphs of anabelioids; non-geometric outer representations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mochizuki (semi-graphs of anabelioids, 2006); Hoshi–Mochizuki (combinatorial anabelian geometry, nodally nondegenerate outer representations, 2009-)
ideas.where_published: Longue Marche (1981) discusses Galois actions and degenerations generally; this specific 'principle' is not in published texts as far as I know

ideas.what: Exercise: find outer actions 'already geometric' in a weak sense but not geometric
ideas.modern_name: geometricity criteria for outer Galois representations; quasi-geometric vs geometric (cf. Hoshi's work on nongeometric sections/representations)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly abandons a programme to make his degeneration-produced outer actions faithful. He also leaves as an exercise constructing 'already geometric' outer actions that are not geometric, which is an early formulation of the problem of characterizing geometric outer Galois representations.
missed.quote: pas par cette voie : faire des actions effectives, exercice : actions ext. déjà géométriques, qui ne soient elles-mêmes géométriques
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical precursor to the combinatorial anabelian geometry of Hoshi–Mochizuki and to work on non-geometric outer representations. The field has since developed this independently, so it is mainly of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a brief abandoned remark. It anticipates later work on non-geometric outer representations and on fundamental groups of degenerate curves, but contains no construction or result.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'qui[?] effectives' is uncertain (possibly a different short word before 'effectives'). The crossed-out word before 'actions' is illegible ('dans'/'des' uncertain).
Line 3 begins 'ext.' (extérieures) and reads 'ext. déjà géométriques, qui ne soient'.
The transcription is otherwise consistent with the image.
